programme: FGF2 and DNMT3B form a two-arm chronic-injury-response module rather than a single complex: FGF2 signals through FGFR (FGFR3-ERK reactivation in HNSCC) to drive epithelial/stromal proliferation and repair after mucosal injury, while DNMT3B lays down promoter hypermethylation (shown at Rab26 in smoke-exposed airway epithelium, and implicated at CDKN2A/p16 in HNC) that silences protective or tumor-suppressor genes in the same injured epithelium. FGF2 supplies the growth-factor/repair signal, DNMT3B supplies the epigenetic-silencing output of the same chronic-insult response.
role_in_a: In COPD, FGF2 is protective/reparative in the alveolar-airway epithelium after elastase-induced injury (PTD-FGF2 and collagen-binding FGF2 attenuate emphysema in mouse models), while cigarette-smoke-generated ROS drives DNMT3B-mediated promoter hypermethylation (shown for Rab26) in airway epithelial cells, part of the aberrant repair/silencing response accompanying emphysema.
role_in_b: In head and neck cancer, FGF2/FGFR3-ERK signaling reactivation is a growth-promoting axis in HNSCC, and DNMT3B is upregulated by the HPV16/18 E7 oncoprotein and its genetic variants track with p16/CDKN2A promoter methylation in HNC patients, placing DNMT3B in tumor-suppressor silencing.
shared_axis: Tobacco smoke is a documented shared exposure across the aerodigestive tract, chronically injuring both airway and head-neck mucosa (with HPV as an added head-neck-specific insult); this repeated injury plausibly drives a common repair-and-silence response in each tissue separately — FGF2-driven proliferative repair alongside DNMT3B-driven epigenetic silencing — producing emphysematous remodeling in the lung and field-cancerization-type changes in the head and neck, even though no retrieved paper studies both diseases together.
reasoning: Both FGF2 and DNMT3B are independently and specifically placed in COPD and in head and neck cancer by distinct papers, so the module is nameable and grounded rather than invented; but no source addresses the two diseases jointly, so pairing them into one shared axis rests on the tobacco/aerodigestive-injury reasoning rather than on retrieved evidence, which caps this at moderate rather than strong. The remaining concordant factors (PAX7, SIX4, HNF1B, NEUROD1, KDM2B, RXRG, ZNF219, EN2) either have no Open Targets or literature placement in either disease, or (PAX7/SIX4's myogenic partners MYOG, MYF6) are flagged discordant, so they were left out rather than forced into the story.
support: PMID 36882376 — PTD-FGF2 attenuates elastase-induced emphysema and alveolar epithelial injury, placing FGF2 in COPD repair biology; PMID 36584430 — collagen-binding FGF2 given early/late reduces elastase-induced lung injury, reinforcing FGF2's reparative role in COPD; PMID 30343534 — FGFR3-mediated ERK reactivation promotes head and neck squamous cell carcinoma growth, placing FGF/FGFR signaling in HNC; PMID 36610560 — cigarette-smoke ROS drives DNMT3B-mediated Rab26 promoter hypermethylation in airway epithelium, placing DNMT3B in COPD-relevant smoke injury response; PMID 39411320 — HPV16/18 E7 expression upregulates DNMT3B, linking an HNC oncogenic driver to DNMT3B induction; PMID 20514408 — DNMT3B polymorphism interacts with age and p16/CDKN2A promoter methylation in head and neck cancer patients, placing DNMT3B in HNC epigenetic silencing.
how_to_falsify: In smoke-exposed airway epithelial organoids and in matched HPV+/HPV- HNSCC lines, block FGF2/FGFR signaling and independently inhibit DNMT3B, then check whether methylation at shared silenced loci (e.g. CDKN2A/Rab26 orthologs) and epithelial repair/proliferation phenotypes move together; also test epidemiologically whether COPD patients show elevated incidence of upper-aerodigestive-tract cancer versus smoking-matched non-COPD controls. If the two arms are uncoupled in the tissue models, or COPD confers no excess HNC risk beyond shared smoking exposure, the shared-axis account fails.
caveats: Findings are drawn from 598 patient-group comparisons across only 2 independent cohort pairs, so cohort-level replication is limited to two studies even though many subgroup comparisons exist within them; FGF2 was concordant in 179/598 (~30%) and DNMT3B in 155/598 (~26%) of comparisons, well under half. MYOG and MYF6, which would extend this into a full myogenic-differentiation story with PAX7/SIX4, are explicitly discordant here and were excluded rather than folded in. Only a single-view exclusion list was supplied for this pair (IRX4, TCF15, TCF7L2, ZXDC, PPARGC1B, NKX3-1, KLF13, HOXA5, ZFX, NFX1, ZIC2, TADA2A); no tissue-generic exclusion list was provided, so that filter cannot be checked here. Tissue pairing is head_neck|lung, anatomically and etiologically linked mainly through shared inhaled-carcinogen exposure of the aerodigestive tract, not through direct tissue contiguity.
